title: Folic acid tablets, USP (1 mg), Rx only: prescribing information
authors: Amneal Pharmaceuticals of New York LLC; US Food and Drug Administration
journal: DailyMed, US National Library of Medicine; ANDA 040625, label effective 15 April 2026
result: Indicated for megaloblastic anaemias due to folate deficiency and anaemias of nutritional origin, pregnancy, infancy or childhood. Warning: folic acid alone is improper therapy for pernicious anaemia and other megaloblastic anaemias in which vitamin B12 is deficient. Precautions: doses above 0.1 mg daily may obscure pernicious anaemia, haematologic remission occurring while neurologic manifestations remain progressive, which may result in severe nervous system damage before the correct diagnosis is made. Interactions: folic acid antagonises the anticonvulsant action of phenytoin. Adverse reactions: allergic sensitisation after oral and parenteral use, including erythema, rash, itching, malaise and bronchospasm, and one case suggesting anaphylaxis after injection; at 15 mg daily for 1 month, gastrointestinal effects and altered sleep, difficulty concentrating, irritability, overactivity, excitement, depression, confusion and impaired judgment; decreased serum vitamin B12 with prolonged therapy; in an uncontrolled study, more seizures in some epileptic patients taking phenobarbital, primidone or phenytoin. Overdosage section: except in pregnancy and lactation, therapeutic doses above 0.4 mg daily should not be given until pernicious anaemia has been ruled out. Dosage: doses above 0.1 mg should not be used unless B12-deficiency anaemia has been ruled out or is adequately treated; daily doses above 1 mg do not enhance the haematologic effect, and most of the excess is excreted unchanged in urine. Long-term carcinogenicity, mutagenicity and fertility studies in animals have not been conducted.
